workingGrids.name: Victoria Stone Works open working grid
workingGrids.classification: Mapped open twenty-cell working grid; exact apparatus unresolved
workingGrids.planEvidence: Five columns and four rows of unshaded cells east of the diagonally hatched Victoria Stone western shed. Native wall/line crossings were inspected individually; the source building extract contains no polygon for the grid. Keep all interiors open and the neighbouring access lanes clear.
workingGrids.heightEvidence: No added elevation. Boundaries are drawn on the existing ground surface; apparatus height is not established by the OS plan.
workingGrids.appearanceEvidence: Line width and stone/ground colour are interpreted display choices, not measured wall thickness or identified construction material. No roof, enclosure, tank contents or exact production process is asserted.

tracks.profileEvidence: The OS fixes plan geometry and has local benchmarks around 14–18 ft, but does not establish this model grade. Hold existing branch formation of 5.5 m over a shared level approach derived from all siding intersections with both the ordinary and northern-connection branch banks, including sleeper width and a full station margin. This prevents rails disappearing below the existing bank/ballast. Keep a long linear 240 m transition farther outward, resolving the inherited level difference at about 1:44. Equal graph distance gives shared junctions identical formation and rail-top levels. These levels and earth slopes are explicit model interpretations, not an original railway gradient.
tracks.evidence: OS coal/depot siding fan re-read west of Stratford Market roofs. One western track and five paired stems; pair spacing, rail profile and yard-level elevation interpreted. Existing Woolwich and main railway routes remain fixed. Complete mapped throat retained beyond yard-parcel limits; exact branch-track join uses saved junction register. No Goad evidence asserted.

evidence: Parcel and building geometry from the existing GIS/map register. Surface materials, wear, damp patches and small stock groups are typological visual interpretations. Routes describe clear circulation space, not identified historical gates or roads.
